blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Aligning large language models (LLMs) to diverse user preferences is fundamentally hindered by standard alignment paradigms that optimize for monolithic users. In this work, empirical studies are first used to reveal the existence of a massive, untapped performance headroom for personalized generation through test-time alignment. We demonstrate that personalized generation is uniquely suited for test-time scaling methods like Best-of- N N (BoN) because it can be viewed primarily as a candidate matching problem rather than a generator capability bottleneck. While reward models could in principle exploit this headroom, they are poorly calibrated for personalization, and their billion-parameter scale makes scoring large candidate pools prohibitively expensive. To overcome this limitation, we propose a parameter-efficient framework utilizing million-parameter scale multi-layer perceptron (MLP) ranking models. Our personalized ranking model directly reuses the internal embeddings of the base generator with minimal overhead. By scaling train-time data to provide fine-grained personalized preferences, this million-parameter ranking model accurately scores large candidate pools and can seamlessly guide generation to reduce the cost of materializing N N candidates. Extensive experiments on nine datasets spanning three personalized generation settings show that our personalized ranking model effectively exploits the discovered headroom, outperforming billion-parameter generalist reward models on every dataset, with under 0.4% of their parameters and four orders of magnitude lower scoring latency.
blocks.zh: 将大型语言模型(LLMs)与多样化的用户偏好保持一致,从根本上受到标准对齐范式的阻碍,这些范式是对单一用户的优化. 在这项工作中,经验研究首先用来揭示存在一个庞大的,未开发的性能主室,通过测试时间对接实现个性化生成. 我们证明,个性化一代特别适合测试时间的缩放方法,如Best-Of-N N(BON),因为它主要可以被视为一个候选匹配问题,而不是发电机能力瓶颈。 虽然奖励模式原则上可以利用这个头室,但是它们对于个性化的校准很差,其10亿参数的尺度使得大候选人池的评分过高。 为了克服这一限制,我们建议采用一个参数效率高的框架,利用百万参数尺度的多层透视模型。 我们的个性化排位模型 直接重新使用底部发电机的内部嵌入 最小的间接费用。 通过缩放列车时间数据提供精细的个性化偏好,这个百万参数的排名模型准确评分了大候选人池,可以无缝地指导生成,降低NN候选人的实现成本. 跨越三个个性化世代设置的9个数据集的广泛实验显示,我们个性化的排名模型有效地利用了发现的头室,在每个数据集上表现优于十亿参数的通用奖赏模型,其参数的0.4%以下,四个星级的积分低等.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: As large language models (LLMs) are deployed in increasingly subjective settings, from writing in a user’s voice to explaining why an item suits them, the assumption behind standard alignment begins to bind. Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) and its variants [ 20 , 1 ] have proven highly effective at instilling general alignment, but they do so under the assumption of a single, monolithic set of human preferences. Human preferences are pluralistic [ 31 , 27 ] , and a monolithic reward averages away exactly the idiosyncratic choices that make a response read as if it were written for a particular person [ 17 , 40 , 9 , 22 ] .
blocks.zh: 由于大型语言模型(LLMs)被部署在越来越主观的环境下,从用用户的声音写到解释一个项目为什么适合它们,标准校正背后的假设开始绑定. 从人类反馈中强化学习(RLHF)及其变体[20,1]已证明在灌输一般对齐方面非常有效,但他们这样做是基于一种单一的人类偏好。 人类的偏好是多元的[31,27],单曲的奖励平均会完全远离那些做出回应的特异性选择,仿佛是写给特定人的[17,40,9,22].

blocks.en: The prevailing response treats this as a capability deficit of the generator and repairs it at training time, by finetuning per user or learning to adapt the generator from user data [ 10 , 32 ] . We start from a different question: Does the base model already have the capability of producing well-personalized responses that we are failing to pick out? Figure 1 answers with an oracle experiment. When the evaluation metric itself selects the best of N N sampled candidates, alignment with the user’s own reference keeps improving as the pool grows; in contrast, when a state-of-the-art reward model selects instead, it plateaus almost immediately and captures only a small fraction of the available gain. The oracle shows that well-matched candidates are already in the pool, whereas naively using the reward model cannot find them: the capability is in the generator, and the bottleneck is selection .
blocks.zh: 普遍的反应将此视为发电机能力不足的情况,并在培训时对其进行修理,办法是对每个用户进行微调,或学习如何根据用户数据调整发电机[10,32]。 我们从另一个问题开始: 基础模型是否已经有能力产生我们未能挑选出来的个性化反应? 图1用甲骨文实验解答. 当评价衡量标准本身选择N N 抽样候选人中最好的候选人时,随着池子的增多,与用户自身参考的配合不断改善;相反,当一个最先进的奖励模式选择了,它几乎立即固定下来,只获取了可用收益的一小部分。 预言显示, 合适的候选人已经进入人才库, 而天真地使用奖励模式却找不到他们:

blocks.en: Exploiting this headroom with a standard reward model is costly in two ways. A reward model is a separate billion-parameter transformer, so scoring a pool means re-encoding the same prompt and every candidate from scratch: selection cost grows with N N , with response length, and with the reward model’s width, and in our measurements scoring a pool with an 8B reward model costs about as much as generating it. Beyond cost, generalist reward models are trained to rank responses by universal qualities, and Figure 1 shows this is the wrong yardstick for a pool whose candidates are all fluent and all on topic but differ in whose voice they are written in.
blocks.zh: 用标准奖励模式来利用这个头室在两种方式上代价高昂. 一个奖励模型是一个单独的十亿参数的变压器,因此评分池意味着从头开始重新编码同样的即时和每个候选人:选择成本随着N N 、 响应长度和奖励模型的宽度而增加,在我们测量中,评分一个8B奖励模型的成本与生成成本一样高。 除了成本外,一般奖赏模式还经过培训,按照普世素质对回应进行排序,图1显示,这是对一个人才库的错误衡量标准,其候选人都是流利的,而且都讲题目,但其声音却各不相同。

blocks.en: We therefore decouple selection from language understanding. The generator has already read the query, the user profile, and each candidate, and its final-layer hidden states carry that understanding; we read those states directly and train a small multi-layer perceptron (MLP) of 1M to 30M parameters to map them to a scalar score. No text is re-encoded and no per-user parameters are learned. Because the ranker operates in a fixed feature space, it cannot learn a representation of its own; whatever it learns about a user’s choices must come from the supervision. We build that supervision from the generator itself. For each training prompt we sample a pool of candidates and label every candidate with its ROUGE-L against the reference the user actually wrote. The pool supplies realistic hard negatives, responses that are well formed but not what this user would have written, and pointwise regression on these labels calibrates the ranker for exactly the selection task it faces at test time. The loss itself is not the point: pairwise and listwise objectives perform comparably.
blocks.zh: 因此,我们将选择与语言理解脱钩。 生成器已经读取了查询,用户简介,以及每个候选者,其最终层隐藏状态都带有这种理解;我们直接读取这些状态,并训练1M到30M参数的小型多层感知器(MLP),将其映射到一个标分. 没有文本重新编码,也没有获得每个用户的参数。 由于分级器在固定的特性空间中运行,它不能学习自己的代表;无论它了解什么用户的选择,都必须来自监督. 我们从发电机本身建立监督系统。 每一次训练,我们都会抽查一组候选人,并将每个候选人用ROUGE-L与用户实际写的参考书名进行标签。 集合提供了现实的硬底片,反应形成良好,但不是这个用户会写的东西,并且在这些标签上指向回归,校准了排位符,以准确反映其在测试时面临的选择任务. 损失本身不是问题所在:对等和列表式目标具有可比性。

blocks.en: With selection nearly free, the remaining cost of Best-of- N N is the pool itself: every candidate must be fully generated before it can be scored. This raises the question of whether the ranker can act before the pool exists. Because it scores candidates from the generator’s own hidden states, it can steer decoding directly: when the generator is uncertain about the next token, we nudge its choice toward what the ranker predicts the user would prefer. This recovers part of the selection gain at the cost of a single generation; most of the headroom still requires scoring a pool, so we present guided decoding as a complement to selection rather than a replacement for it.
blocks.zh: 由于选手几乎是免费的,Best-Of-N的剩余成本是游泳池本身:每个候选人必须全部产生才能得分. 这提出了军衔者是否可以在水池存在之前采取行动的问题. 因为它对来自生成器自身隐藏状态的候选者进行评分,它可以直接引导解码:当生成器不确定下一个信号时,我们将其选择转向排序器预测用户会喜欢的东西。 这收回了一部分选择收益,而牺牲了一代人;多数头室仍然需要打分池,所以我们提出指导解码作为选择的补充而不是替代.

blocks.en: We evaluate on nine datasets spanning three personalized generation settings: short-form personalized generation [ 28 ] , long-form personalized question answering [ 29 ] , and personalized explainable recommendation [ 18 ] . Our ranker has a few million parameters; the reward models it is compared against have eight billion. Against four generalist reward models, it is nonetheless the best selector on every dataset and keeps improving with the pool size where they plateau or decline. We then finetune the best of those reward models per dataset on the same candidate pools with the same objective, which sets the ceiling a model of that size can reach on this task. The finetuned model is ahead, as it should be, but the ranker recovers most of its gain with a model more than two hundred times smaller, at orders of magnitude lower latency, and without finetuning a billion-parameter model for every dataset. Without any preference labels, it also matches personalized reward models that fit per-user parameters from labeled comparisons, and its selections transfer to a metric it was never trained on.
blocks.zh: 我们评价了9个数据集,涵盖三个个性化的一代:短式个性化一代[28],长式个性化问题回答[29],以及个性化的可解释建议[18]。 我们的军衔有几百万个参数;与之相比的奖励模型有80亿。 相对于4个通用奖励模式,它仍然是每个数据集中最好的选择者,并且随着其高原或下降的池大小不断改善。 然后,我们调整同一候选人集合中每个数据集的最佳奖励模式,以达到相同目标,从而设定了这种规模的上限。 微调模型在前方,应该如此,但分级器以一个模型小于200倍以上,在数量级低的空位级上,恢复其大部分收益,并且没有为每个数据集微调10亿参数模型. 它没有任何优惠标签,它也匹配符合每个用户参数的个性化奖励模型,从标签上的比较,其选择转移到从未受过训练的衡量标准。

blocks.en: In summary, our main contributions are summarized as follows: • Empirical Discovery of Personalization Headroom: An oracle Best-of- N N analysis shows that the base generator already produces well-personalized candidates while generalist reward models recover only a small fraction of the gain, reframing personalized alignment as a candidate selection problem. • Introduce Personalized Ranking Model: A million-parameter MLP that reuses the generator’s own hidden states in place of a billion-parameter reward model. Trained on candidate pools with realistic negatives, it outperforms generalist reward models over two hundred times its size and extends to single-pass guided decoding. • Comprehensive Experimental Validation: Extensive evaluations across nine datasets and three paradigms demonstrate that our million-parameter MLP recovers most of the gain of explicitly finetuned, billion-parameter SOTA reward models at a fraction of their size and inference cost, and matches personalized reward models without per-user preference labels.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: RLHF [ 20 , 1 ] and DPO [ 26 ] align LLMs to a monolithic notion of preference through reward models trained with the Bradley-Terry objective [ 3 ] . This averages out pluralistic tastes, and a Bradley-Terry reward is identified only up to a prompt-dependent shift, so its scores are not calibrated across the large candidate pools that test-time selection must compare [ 41 ] . We instead frame personalization as candidate matching and train a lightweight ranking model on the generator’s own embeddings with a pointwise objective. The objective itself is not a contribution: pairwise and listwise alternatives perform comparably under the same architecture and data (Appendix B.1 ).
blocks.zh: RLHF[20,1]和DPO[26]通过与布拉德利-泰瑞目标训练的奖励模式,将LLMs与单一的偏好概念联系起来[3]. 这个平均数淘汰了多元口味,一个布拉德利-泰瑞奖赏只被确定到一个迅速依赖的转变,因此其分数没有在测试时间选择必须比较的大型候选人集合中校准[41]. 我们将个性化设定为候选人匹配, 目标本身并不是一种贡献:在相同的架构和数据下,对等和列表式的替代品具有可比性(附录B.1 )。

blocks.en: Early work injects persona descriptions or retrieved history into the prompt [ 38 , 28 ] or fine-tunes per user [ 10 , 32 ] , treating personalization as a generator deficit. A second line personalizes the reward model: PAL [ 9 ] , VPL [ 22 ] , PReF [ 30 ] , and LoRe [ 2 ] place each user in a low-dimensional preference space that is fit or inferred from labeled pairwise comparisons, while GPO [ 40 ] and SynthesizeMe [ 27 ] adapt an LLM judge from a user’s labeled examples. All of them require per-user preference annotations and, as deployed, a separate encoder pass per candidate. Our ranker needs neither: it derives the user signal from the interaction history already present in the generation context and recycles the generator’s hidden states. Appendix B.2 compares against all six on XRec, the setting in which per-user supervision can be constructed.
blocks.zh: 早期的工作注入了人物a描述或检索历史到每个用户[38,28]或微调[10,32],将个性化视为发电机的不足. 第二行将奖励模式个性化:PAL [9],VPL [22],PReF [30],和Lore [2] 将每个用户置于一个低维偏好空间,该空间适合或从标签对等的比较中推断出来,而GPO [40] 和Synthesize Me [27] 则从用户的标签示例中修改一个LLM判断. 所有这些都需要每个用户的首选说明,而且按照部署,每个候选人需要单独的编码员通行证。 我们的排行符不需要:它从生成背景中已经存在的交互历史中获取用户信号,并回收生成器隐藏状态。 附录B.2比较了XRec上的所有6个,即可以构建每个用户监管的设置.

blocks.en: Scaling inference compute can rival scaling model size [ 19 , 37 ] . Best-of- N N sampling and guided decoding [ 35 , 11 , 36 , 8 , 12 ] rely on a reward model to select or steer and inherit its per-candidate encoding cost; even the lightest of them, FUDGE’s future discriminators, re-encode the partial sequence with their own network rather than reading the generator’s states, and all target a single monolithic reward rather than an individual user. UserAlign [ 21 ] and T-POP [ 24 ] personalize at inference time but elicit preferences through interactive pairwise queries cast as bandits, whereas our ranker issues no queries and needs no labels beyond the user’s existing history. Our ranker brings the selection cost to near zero by scoring the generator’s own hidden states, and because it is differentiable in those states it can also steer decoding directly.

blocks.en: 3 Methodology
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en: In this section, we formalize the personalized test-time alignment problem and introduce our parameter-efficient, decoupled ranking framework. We begin by defining the core objective of Best-of- N N sampling and identifying the severe computational bottlenecks inherent in standard reward models. Subsequently, we detail our lightweight ranking architecture and the preference optimization strategy tailored specifically for learning personal preferences. We conclude with an asymptotic efficiency analysis to theoretically validate the massive scalability of our approach. An overview of our methodology is illustrated in Figure 2 .
blocks.zh: 在这一节中,我们正式确定了个性化的测试时间对接问题,并引入了我们的参数效率高,脱钩的排名框架. 我们首先确定最佳N抽样的核心目标,并查明标准奖励模式固有的严重计算瓶颈。 随后,我们详细介绍了我们轻量级的排名结构和专门为学习个人喜好量身定制的首选优化策略. 最后,我们进行不对称效率分析,从理论上证实我们的方法可以大规模扩展。 图2概述了我们的方法。

blocks.en: 3.1 Problem Formulation: Personalized Test-time Alignment
blocks.zh: 3.1 问题表述:个性化测试时间调整

blocks.en: Let U U denote a set of users, X X the space of input prompts, and Y Y the space of generated responses. In standard generalized alignment, the goal is to optimize a policy π θ ​ ( y | x ) \pi_{\theta}(y|x) that maximizes a globally shared reward. However, in personalized alignment, the objective shifts to finding an optimal user-specific policy π ∗ ​ ( y | x , u ) \pi^{*}(y|x,u) that caters to the idiosyncratic preferences of user u ∈ U u\in U .

Instead of actively finetuning the base policy π θ \pi_{\theta} for every user, test-time alignment employs Best-of- N N (BoN) sampling. Given a prompt x x , the base generator samples a diverse candidate pool of N N responses, denoted as C = { y 1 , y 2 , … , y N } C=\{y_{1},y_{2},\dots,y_{N}\} . The objective is to learn a personalized scoring function, r ^ u ​ ( x , y ) \hat{r}_{u}(x,y) , which identifies the optimal candidate y ∗ y^{*} that maximizes the user’s implicit utility: y ∗ = arg ⁡ max y i ∈ C ​ r ^ u ​ ( x , y i ) y^{*}=\arg\max_{y_{i}\in C}\hat{r}_{u}(x,y_{i}) (1) In standard paradigms, r ^ u ​ ( x , y ) \hat{r}_{u}(x,y) is parameterized as a massive LLM. Executing Equation 1 requires N N independent, full forward passes through this heavyweight encoder, creating a severe computational bottleneck that limits the feasible size of N N and, consequently, the ability to exploit the personalization headroom.

blocks.en: 3.2 Personalized Ranking Model
blocks.zh: 3.2 个人定级模式

blocks.en: To eradicate the redundancy of secondary encoding, we decouple the language understanding component from the preference scoring component. The base LLM generator has already comprehended the prompt x x and synthesized the response y i y_{i} , so its internal representations already contain dense, high-quality semantic features. Rather than re-encoding the text, our framework directly reads the generator’s own final-layer hidden states.
blocks.zh: 为了消除二次编码的冗余,我们将语言理解部分与偏好评分部分脱钩. 基础 LLM 生成器已经理解了 exx 并且合成了反应 y y y i i },所以其内部表达已经包含密集,高质量的语义特征. 我们的框架不是重新编码文本,而是直接读取生成器自身的最终层隐藏状态。

blocks.en: Three texts take part in personalized generation: the task query x x , the user profile u u , and the sampled response y i y_{i} . The profile is the user’s interaction history as provided by the benchmark: retrieved history items for LaMP and LaMP-QA, and a pre-written user summary for XRec. For each of the three texts we take the generator’s final-layer hidden state at its last token, denoted h x , h u , h y i ∈ ℝ d h_{x},h_{u},h_{y_{i}}\in\mathbb{R}^{d} , where d d is the hidden dimension (the last hidden token in Figure 2 ). Appendix C specifies the profile text used for each benchmark and how the embeddings are extracted in our implementation.

It is the generator’s own summary of the profile text, so the same frozen model that writes the response also represents the user. Because h x h_{x} and h u h_{u} depend only on the prompt, they are computed once per query and shared across all N N candidates.

blocks.zh: 3.3 点偏好优化

blocks.en: The ranking model f ϕ f_{\phi} is agnostic to the training objective: any differentiable ranking loss can be applied to the recycled embeddings of Section 3.2 . We adopt pointwise regression by default. Let s ∗ ​ ( x , y i , u ) ∈ ℝ s^{*}(x,y_{i},u)\in\mathbb{R} denote the target utility of candidate y i y_{i} for user u u . We minimize ℒ MSE ​ ( ϕ ) = 𝔼 ( x , y i , u ) ∼ 𝒟 ​ [ ( f ϕ ​ ( h x , h u , h y i ) − s ∗ ​ ( x , y i , u ) ) 2 ] \mathcal{L}_{\text{MSE}}(\phi)=\mathbb{E}_{(x,y_{i},u)\sim\mathcal{D}}\left[\left(f_{\phi}(h_{x},h_{u},h_{y_{i}})-s^{*}(x,y_{i},u)\right)^{2}\right] (3) which maps every candidate onto a shared, absolute utility scale.

In practice we standardize s ∗ s^{*} within each candidate pool, to zero mean and unit variance over the N N candidates of a prompt. Best-of- N N selection is invariant to per-prompt shifts, so this focuses the regression on within-pool discrimination rather than on predicting each prompt’s overall difficulty.
blocks.zh: 在实践中,我们把每个候选人库内的S = = = = 改为零,单位差异大于N N候选人。 N最佳选手对每时每刻的转变无动于衷,因此,这把回归的焦点放在池内的歧视上,而不是预测每个球员的总体困难。

blocks.en: Two properties of our setting favor pointwise regression. First, our supervision is cardinal rather than ordinal: each candidate carries an absolute target, whereas pairwise or listwise objectives are invariant to monotone transformations of the targets and therefore discard how much better one candidate is than another. Second, Best-of- N N selection and the guided decoding of Section 3.4 consume absolute utilities that must be comparable across large pools, whereas pairwise scores are identified only up to prompt-dependent shifts. Pointwise training also scales as 𝒪 ⁡ ( N ) \mathcal{O}(N) per prompt rather than 𝒪 ⁡ ( N 2 ) \mathcal{O}(N^{2}) for all-pairs objectives.
blocks.zh: 我们设置的两个属性 顺理成章的回归。 第一,我们的监督是首要的,而不是普通的:每个候选人都有绝对目标,而双向或逐项目标则无法改变目标的单一变化,因此放弃一个候选人比另一个候选人好多少。 第二,N节最佳选手和第3.4节的制导解码消耗的绝对公用设施必须在整个大池中具有可比性,而双向计分只确定为即时调值。 尖端训练也以 O \\ (N)\ mathcal{(N)\ mathcal{(N)) / prooper / 而不是 O \ (N 2)\ mathcal{(N)} 为全方位目标进行。

blocks.en: Alternatives include the pairwise Bradley-Terry objective standard in reward modeling [ 3 ] and RankNet [ 5 ] , and listwise objectives such as ListNet [ 7 ] , ListMLE [ 34 ] , and LambdaRank [ 4 ] . Appendix B.1 compares these objectives under identical architecture, data, and protocol. All objectives perform comparably, so pointwise MSE is a well-founded default rather than a requirement, and the gains of our framework stem from embedding recycling and train-time candidate scaling rather than from the choice of loss.

blocks.en: To ensure this minimal architecture achieves high discriminative power, data construction is paramount. Rather than utilizing randomly sampled negative responses, we populate the training distribution 𝒟 \mathcal{D} with candidates directly generated by the base LLM generator π θ \pi_{\theta} . The target utility s ∗ ​ ( x , y i , u ) s^{*}(x,y_{i},u) is the downstream evaluation metric of y i y_{i} against the reference authored by user u u (ROUGE-L in our experiments). This strategy yields hard negatives: responses that are structurally sound and factually correct, but stylistically or semantically misaligned with the specific user u u , and therefore receive low targets. Training the ranking model to minimize the MSE over these hard negatives bridges the representation gap typically associated with low-parameter models.

blocks.en: 3.5 Time Complexity Analysis
blocks.zh: 3.5 时间复杂性分析

blocks.en: The primary advantage of our decoupled architecture lies in its asymptotic test-time efficiency.
blocks.zh: 我们脱钩建筑的主要优势在于它的不对称测试时间效率.

blocks.en: Consider a standard Best-of- N N scenario where candidate responses have an average sequence length of L L . For a standard heavyweight reward model, selecting the best candidate requires passing the prompt and response through the full transformer stack N N times. The time complexity for the selection phase scales as 𝒪 ⁡ ( N ⋅ L ⋅ d r 2 ) \mathcal{O}(N\cdot L\cdot d_{r}^{2}) , where d r d_{r} is the hidden dimension of the reward model. As N N grows to exploit the personalization headroom, this linear scaling with respect to sequence length and full model dimensionality becomes prohibitively expensive.
blocks.zh: 考虑一个标准 候选人答复的平均序列长度为LL的N N最佳设想。 对于标准的重量级奖励模型,选择最佳候选人需要通过全变压器堆栈N时间通过即时和响应. 选择阶段比例表作为 O +⁡ (N L → d r 2 )\ mathcal{O}(N\cdot L\cdot d_{r}^{2})的时间复杂度,其中d r d_{r}是奖励模式的隐藏维度. 随着NN逐渐利用个性化头室,这种与序列长度和完整的模型维度有关的线性缩放变得极为昂贵。

blocks.en: In contrast, our proposed framework operates with an 𝒪 ⁡ ( 1 ) \mathcal{O}(1) amortized encoding cost. The generation of the N N embeddings occurs naturally during the candidate generation phase. The subsequent ranking step merely requires a forward pass through the shallow MLP for each candidate. The time complexity for selection is thus reduced to 𝒪 ⁡ ( N ⋅ d 2 ) \mathcal{O}(N\cdot d^{2}) , completely independent of the sequence length L L , where d d is the hidden dimension of the LLM generator. Because d 2 ≪ L ⋅ d r 2 d^{2}\ll L\cdot d_{r}^{2} , the latency overhead introduced by our ranker is virtually negligible. This theoretical efficiency allows our method to scale to large candidate pools in real-time deployments with negligible computational cost; Appendix C.4 reports measured latency and memory.

blocks.en: 4 Experiments
blocks.zh: 4 实验

blocks.en: 4.1 Experimental Settings
blocks.zh: 4.1 实验设置

blocks.en: We use Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct [ 25 ] as the generative backbone. Following the benchmark protocols, we evaluate with ROUGE-L [ 13 ] against the gold reference, and use ROUGE-1 as a check where noted. In all nine datasets the reference is authored by the target user, so lexical overlap with it measures alignment with that user’s revealed stylistic choices rather than generic quality; semantic metrics such as BERTScore [ 39 ] abstract away precisely the surface-level nuances in which personalization manifests. Because the ranker is trained on ROUGE-L targets, we additionally report BLEU [ 23 ] in Section 4.3 as a held-out metric, verifying that its gains reflect learned user preference rather than regression to the training metric.
blocks.zh: 我们用Quen2.5-7B-指示[25]作为基因骨干. 按照基准协议,我们与ROUGE-L[13]对照黄金参考值进行评估,并使用ROUGE-1作为注明位置的检查. 在所有9个数据集中,参考文献都由目标用户编写,因此词汇学上与它重叠,用来衡量与该用户所揭示的风格选择的一致性,而不是通用的质量;语义学的衡量标准,如BERTScore[39] 抽象地消除了个人化所表现的表层细微差别。 由于分级员接受关于ROUGE-L目标的培训,我们又在第4.3节中将BLEU[23]作为一个搁置度量衡报告,证实其成绩反映的是学到的用户偏好,而不是回到培训度量衡。

blocks.en: We evaluate our approach using several state-of-the-art discriminative reward models (RMs) as ranking baselines: • Skywork-Reward-V2-Llama-3.1-8B [ 14 ] : A data-centric RM trained on the Skywork-Reward Preference 80K dataset, which focuses on high-quality curated pairs and utilizes a robust vanilla Bradley-Terry (BT) loss to maximize reward differences. • internlm2-7b-reward [ 6 ] : A model trained on a large-scale corpus of 2.4 million preference samples (human and AI-synthesized), providing comprehensive coverage across diverse areas including dialogue, coding, and mathematics. • URM-LLaMa-3.1-8B [ 16 ] : An uncertainty-aware reward model that implements attribute-specific value heads to predict the parameters of a normal distribution, allowing for the estimation of reward reliability. • ArmoRM-Llama3-8B-v0.1 [ 33 ] : An Absolute-Rating Multi-Objective RM that employs a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) gating mechanism to scalarize 19 distinct reward dimensions (e.g., helpfulness, correctness, and verbosity) into a single preference score. Every reward model scores exactly the input our ranker sees: the generation prompt, which carries the query and the user’s retrieved profile, together with the candidate response. Personalization signal is therefore available to these models in context, and what we test is whether generically trained preference models can exploit it when ranking large candidate pools. Section 4.3 adds a second, stronger tier in which the best of them is finetuned on our personalized training distribution.
blocks.zh: 我们使用几种最先进的歧视性奖励模式(RM)作为排名基准来评价我们的方法: • Skywork-Reward-V2-Llama-3.1-8B [14]: 一个以数据为中心的RM在Skywork-Reward Preference 80K数据集上进行了培训,该RM侧重于高品质的配对,并利用强力的香草布拉德利-特里(BT)损失来尽量扩大奖励差异. • 实习生2-7b奖金 [6]: 培训了240万个大宗首选样本(人和人工合成)的模型,全面覆盖包括对话、编码和数学在内的不同领域。 • URM-LLaMa-3.1-8B [16]: 一种认识到不确定性的奖励模型,它执行属性特定价值头来预测正常分布的参数,从而可以估计奖励的可靠性. • ArmoRM-Llama3-8B-v0.1 [33]:一个绝对的RM多目标RM,它使用一种专家混合(MoE)配位机制,将19个不同的奖励维度(如帮助、正确和verbosity)缩小为单一的优惠分数。 每个奖赏模型都得分精确的我们分级员所看到的输入:代号即时,它包含查询和用户检索的配置图,以及候选人的答复。 因此,这些模型在上下文中可以获得个性化信号,我们测试的是,一般训练的偏好模型在排出大候选人群时是否可以加以利用。 第4.3节增加了一个更强的二级,其中最优秀的等级调整了我们的个性化培训分布。

blocks.en: Our evaluation spans nine datasets across three distinct personalization categories: 1. Short-form Personalized Generation (LaMP) [ 28 ] : We focus on three generative tasks requiring models to adapt to user historical profiles: personalized news headline generation (News), scholarly title generation (Scholarly), and tweet paraphrasing (Tweet). 2. Long-form Personalized QA (LaMP-QA) [ 29 ] : This benchmark evaluates informational seeking tasks across three categories: Arts & Entertainment, Lifestyle & Personal Development, and Society & Culture, using personalized rubrics extracted from user narratives. 3. Personalized Explainable Recommendation (XRec) [ 18 ] : We utilize three domain-specific datasets: Amazon, Yelp and Google, to generate natural language explanations for user-item interactions based on collaborative signals and user profiles. The size of the user profiles shipped with these benchmarks varies by more than an order of magnitude, from a median of eight interactions per user on XRec to a median of 143 article–headline pairs on News; following each benchmark’s protocol, only a small retrieved subset (three items for LaMP, six for LaMP-QA) or a pre-written summary (XRec) enters the prompt. Appendix C.1 gives self-contained task descriptions, and Table 6 the per-dataset profile statistics.

blocks.en: 4.2 Main Results
blocks.zh: 4.2 主要成果

blocks.en: Figure 4: Personalized ranking model size against a finetuned reward model at Best-of-64. Points are means over the three datasets of each task, bars span the per-dataset minimum and maximum.

blocks.en: Oracle Best-of- N N selection picks the candidate with the evaluation metric itself and therefore upper-bounds any selector. Against it we place, at each N N , the best of the four generalist reward models of Section 4.1 . Figure 1 shows both averaged per task; Appendix A.1 gives all nine datasets (Figure 5 ). The oracle rises steadily up to N = 64 N=64 on every task, with no sign of saturation, so the generator keeps producing better-matched candidates as the pool grows. The best reward model does not follow. It plateaus by N = 16 N=16 on short-form generation and never beats its N = 1 N=1 score on long-form QA. At N = 64 N=64 it captures at most 23% of the headroom, and under 12% on eight of the nine datasets. Because one curve keeps climbing while the other stays flat, the gap between them widens with N N , and every additional sample adds headroom that a generalist selector fails to exploit. This has three implications. First, much of the personalization we seek does not need to be trained into the generator. A frozen model conditioned on the user’s profile already produces well-matched responses, and what is missing is the ability to recognize them. Second, test-time compute becomes a lever for personalization, but only if the selector’s accuracy scales with the pool. That requires a selector calibrated on the fine, user-specific distinctions among candidates that are all fluent and on topic, rather than on the generic quality differences that generalist reward models are trained to detect. Third, exploiting this headroom requires scoring large pools, so the cost of scoring each candidate becomes the limiting factor. This is what motivates a selector that is both personalized and nearly free to run. The capability is already in the generator; the bottleneck is selection.
blocks.zh: Oracle Best-Of-N选手用评价衡量标准本身来挑选候选人,因此,选择者人数最多。 反之,我们将第4.1节的四大奖赏模式中最好的奖赏放在NN中。 图1显示的是每项任务的平均数据;附录A.1列出所有9个数据集(图5)。 甲骨文在每项任务上稳步上升至N=64N=64,没有饱和的迹象,因此随着池子的增大,发电机不断产生更匹配的候选人. 最好的奖励模式没有遵循。 它在短阵型一代上由N=16N=16高原,在长阵型QA上从未击败过它的N=1N=1分. 在N=64 N=64时,它最多能捕捉23%的头室,9个数据集中的8个不到12%. 由于一个曲线不断攀升,而另一个曲线则保持平坦,它们之间的差距随着N N 的扩大而扩大,每一个额外的样本都添加了一般选手未能利用的头室. 这涉及三个方面。 首先,我们所追求的很多个性化不需要训练成发电机。 以用户的配置为条件的冻结模型已经产生匹配的响应,缺失的是识别它们的能力. 第二,测试时间计算成为个性化的杠杆,但只有在选择者的准确度与游泳池相符的情况下。 这要求选择一个精细的、针对具体用户的区分来校准所有流利的候选人和专题,而不是通用奖赏模式经过培训以发现的一般质量差异。 第三,利用这个头室需要积分大池,所以每个候选人的积分费用成为限制因素. 这激励着一个既个性化又几乎自由运行的选手. 能力已经在生成器中;瓶颈是选择。

blocks.en: Figure 3 compares selectors as N N grows from 1 to 64 (per dataset and per reward model in Figure 6 , Appendix A.2 ). The two families of selectors follow opposite trends. The generalist reward models stay flat or decline as the pool grows, improving only slowly on explainable recommendation. For them, a larger pool is not an opportunity but a risk. Because they reward generic qualities rather than fit to the user, each added candidate is one more chance to select a response that looks good in general but is wrong for this user. Our ranker instead improves steadily with N N on every task, and its advantage over the reward models widens as the pool grows. The first takeaway is that whether test-time compute helps personalization depends entirely on the selector: the same pools yield steady gains under a calibrated ranker and none under a generalist one. The shape of the curve also varies with the task. Gains saturate early on short-form generation, where candidates of a few words differ little from one another, but keep rising on long-form QA and explainable recommendation, where longer responses leave more room for variation. The second takeaway is that pool size should be matched to the task, with small pools sufficient for short outputs and larger ones worthwhile for open-ended responses. We attribute the difference to training on the generator’s own candidate pools, which teaches the ranker the fine-grained distinctions that selection actually requires.
blocks.zh: 图3比较了NN从1增长到64(每个数据集和附录A.2图6中的每个奖励模型)的选定者。 选手的两个家族遵循相反的趋势. 通用奖赏模式随着池子的增大而保持平稳或下降,在可解释的推荐上只缓慢改进. 对他们来说,更大的人才库不是机会,而是风险。 由于它们奖励通用的品质而不是适合用户,每个新增的候选者又是一个选择一般看起来好但对这一用户是错误的反应的机会. 我们的军衔在每一项任务上都稳步提高,NN的军衔,随着球池的扩大,NN对奖励模式的优势也在扩大。 第一个选择是,测试时间的计算是否有助于个性化,完全取决于选择者:同一个池在经过校准的排位器下获得稳定收益,而在通用的排位器下则无。 曲线的形状也随任务而变化. 在短式生成上提前获得饱和度,在短式生成上,几个单词的考生彼此差别不大,但在长式质评和可解释的建议上却不断上升,较长的答复留下了更大的变化空间. 第二项选择是,集合体的规模应与任务相称,小型集合体足以提供短期产出,而大型集合体则足以做出无限制的反应。 我们将此区别归结为在发电机本身的候选人才库上的培训,它教给排位者真正需要的精细区分。

blocks.en: The dashed line marks ranking guided generation, which decodes one response per prompt while the ranker steers uncertain tokens. It reaches the level of Best-of-2 to Best-of-4 of the sampled pool on short-form generation and long-form QA, and of Best-of-1 to Best-of-2 on explainable recommendation, for the cost of a single generation; per dataset it exceeds Best-of-64 only on Tweet and falls below Best-of-1 on News (Figure 6 ). Steering a single trajectory thus recovers a modest part of the selection gain without materializing candidates, while most of the headroom still requires scoring a pool. We conduct a sensitivity analysis by varying each decoding hyperparameter around its default (Appendix C.3 ). ROUGE-L changes by at most about 0.005 on every dataset, so the shared defaults need no per-dataset tuning. Only τ \tau has a visible effect, and it controls how often the ranker intervenes rather than the final score.

blocks.en: 4.3 More Analysis
blocks.zh: 4.3 更多分析

blocks.en: We next ask how much ranker capacity is needed and how the ranker compares with a reward model finetuned for the task. Figure 4 varies the ranker from 1M to 30M parameters and adds Skywork-Reward-V2-Llama-3.1-8B finetuned on the same training pools with the same pointwise objective (Appendix C.2 ); points are means over the three datasets of each task with bars spanning the per-dataset range, and Appendix A.3 gives each dataset (Figure 7 ). Appendix B.2 further compares against personalized reward models that fit user-specific parameters from per-user preference labels.
blocks.zh: 接下来我们问,需要多少军衔能力,军衔与为任务调整的奖励模式相比如何。 图4将排名从1M到30M参数不同,并在同一个训练池上增加了Skywork-Reward-V2-Llama-3.1-8B的微调,并具有相同的点标目标(附录C.2);点标是指每个任务的三个数据集上横跨每个数据集范围的条的点标,附录A.3给出了每个数据集(图7). 附录B.2还比较了符合每个用户偏好标签中用户特定参数的个性化奖励模式.

blocks.en: Ranker size barely matters: from 1M to 30M parameters the Best-of-64 score moves by at most 0.006 ROUGE-L on any dataset, because the semantic work is done by the generator and the ranker only learns a regression in a fixed feature space. The finetuned 8B model is ahead on all nine datasets, by Δ = + 0.019 \Delta=+0.019 ROUGE-L on short-form generation and below + 0.01 +0.01 on long-form QA and explainable recommendation; measured against the headroom, the 30M ranker recovers 45% to 94% of the finetuned model’s gain per dataset. This gap is the price of decoupling. The 8B model re-encodes every candidate and must be finetuned per dataset, whereas the ranker scores recycled embeddings at four orders of magnitude lower cost per query (Appendix C.4 ); for that cost it delivers the bulk of what finetuning a billion-parameter model buys.
blocks.zh: Ranker大小不重要:从1M到30M的参数中,Best-of-64的分数在任意数据集上以最多0.006 ROUGE-L移动,因为语义工作是由生成器完成的,而排位器只在固定特征空间中学习回归. 微调后的8B模型在所有9个数据集上都领先,在短式生成上为+0.019\Delta+0.019 RoUGE-L,在长式QA和可解释推荐上为+0.01+0.01;对照头室进行测量,30M分级器每个数据集恢复微调后的模型收益的45%至94%. 这种差距是脱钩的代价. 8B模型重新编码每个候选者,必须每套数据集进行微调,而排名者对嵌入的分数按四个数量级进行循环,每次查询的成本较低(附录C.4);由于这一成本,它提供了十亿参数模型购买的微调的大部分。

blocks.en: Because the ranker is trained on ROUGE-L targets, one may ask whether it merely regresses the training metric. If so, its advantage should vanish under a metric it never saw. Table 4 therefore evaluates the Best-of-64 selection of every ranker under BLEU, keeping all rankers fixed; ours remains trained solely on ROUGE-L labels. Our ranker selects the highest-BLEU candidate on all nine datasets, and the four generalist reward models trail it everywhere, most clearly on explainable recommendation, where our ranker improves on the strongest baseline by 20% to 64% relative.
blocks.zh: 由于军衔人员接受过关于ROUGE-L目标的培训,人们可能会问,这是否只是使训练标准倒退。 如果是这样的话,它的好处应该用它从未看到过的尺度消失。 因此,表4评价了64年中每一名BLEU级军衔的最佳选择,保持所有军衔的固定;我们的军衔仍然只接受ROUGE-L级的训练。 我们的军衔选手在所有9个数据集中都选择了最高的BLEU候选人,四个通用奖赏模型都追踪到它,最清楚的是在可解释的推荐上,我们的军衔选手在最强的基准上提高了20%到64%的相对比例.

blocks.en: This transfer is not trivial. Table 1 quantifies how differently ROUGE-L and BLEU order the candidates of a pool. The two metrics select the same best candidate in only 12–37% of pools, and their within-pool rank correlation is 0.36–0.59, so a ranker that had memorized the ROUGE-L scoring function would gain little under BLEU. The across-prompt correlation is higher (0.48–0.78), which reflects shared difficulty between prompts rather than agreement on which candidate to pick, and it is the within-pool disagreement that matters for selection. The ranker has therefore learned which candidate comes closest to what the user would have written, a property that transfers across surface metrics. The pattern mirrors the main results: generalist reward models fall short not because the evaluation is n n -gram based, but because they lack calibration for user-authored references, a conclusion now corroborated under a metric none of the rankers was tuned toward.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: We challenged the assumption that personalized LLM alignment requires expensive train-time intervention. An oracle Best-of- N N analysis showed that the base generator already produces well-personalized candidates but generalist reward models fail to select them, which reframes personalized alignment as a candidate selection problem. To solve it at low cost, we introduced a million-parameter MLP ranker that scores candidates directly from the generator’s own hidden states. Trained on the generator’s own candidate pools labeled against user-authored references, it learns the fine-grained distinctions that personalized selection requires. The ranker outperforms generalist 8B reward models on all nine datasets and keeps improving as the pool grows where they stall. It approaches an 8B reward model finetuned per dataset at four orders of magnitude lower scoring latency, and it is competitive with personalized reward models without any per-user preference labels. It can also steer decoding directly, recovering part of the selection gain from a single generation. Since it attaches to any generator that exposes its hidden states, it offers a practical route to per-user alignment without retraining the generator. Our evaluation rests on lexical overlap with user-authored references, and a human study of style consistency is left for future work.
blocks.zh: 我们质疑这样一种假设,即个性化LLM调整需要昂贵的火车时间干预。 一个Oracle Best-Of-N分析显示,基础生成器已经产生了个性化的考生,但通用奖赏模型未能选中他们,这把个性化的校正重新设定为考生选题. 为了以低廉的成本解决它,我们引入了百万参数的MLP排名,直接从发电机本身隐藏状态对候选人进行评分。 它根据用户提供的参考书目,在发电机本身的候选集合中接受培训,学会了个性化选择需要的细微区别。 排名者在所有9个数据集上超越了通论者8B的奖励模型,并随着游泳池的生长而不断改善. 它接近每个数据集的8B奖赏模型,以4个数量级的低评分间隔度进行微调,它与个性化奖赏模型竞争,没有每个用户的首选标签. 它还可以直接引导解码,从单一一代中回收部分选择收益. 由于它附着在任何暴露其隐藏状态的生成器上,它提供了一个不重新训练生成器的每个用户对齐的实际途径. 我们的评价基于与用户授权的参考文献的词汇重叠,关于风格一致性的人类研究留待今后进行。

blocks.en: Table 3 retrains the identical 2.8M-parameter MLP ranker under the pairwise and listwise objectives discussed in Section 3.3 , keeping the architecture, training data, and budget fixed (Appendix C.2 ). MSE regresses to the ROUGE-L target standardized within each candidate pool; Bradley–Terry is trained on sampled candidate pairs and RankNet on all pairs within a pool; ListNet, ListMLE, and LambdaRank consume the ordering of each pool induced by the targets. No single objective dominates: MSE is best on News, ListMLE on Tweet, Lifestyle, and Society, the pairwise objectives on Scholarly, Art, Yelp, and Google, and ListNet on Amazon. The spread across objectives is small, at most 0.012 ROUGE-L on any dataset and below 0.003 on the three explainable recommendation datasets. The objectives that fall furthest behind on the three short-form datasets and on Art and Lifestyle are ListNet and LambdaRank, which were designed for graded ordinal relevance in retrieval. We draw two conclusions. Pointwise MSE is a well-founded default in our setting, since it uses the magnitude information in the cardinal labels and scales linearly in the pool size, but pairwise objectives are not inherently suboptimal here and perform on par. More importantly, the narrow spread confirms that the gains of the framework stem from embedding recycling and train-time candidate scaling rather than from the loss, which we do not claim as a contribution.
blocks.zh: 表3将相同的2.8M参数的MLP分级器重划到第3.3节所讨论的对称和列表目标下,使结构、培训数据和预算保持不变(附录C.2)。 MSE在每一个候选人才库中向ROUGE-L目标退步; Bradley-Terry接受过对候选人才的抽样培训,RankNet接受过对在一个人才库中所有候选人才的抽样培训; ListNet, ListMLE,以及LambdaRank 消耗目标所引导的每个人才库的订单. 没有单一的目标占据主导地位:MSE在News上最好,ListMLE在Tweet上最好,Lifetyle,以及Social,在The Scholarly,Art,Yelp,和Google上对等的目标,在Amazon上的ListNet. 各个目标的分布很小,在任何数据集上最多0.012 ROUGE-L,在三个可解释的建议数据集上低于0.003。 在三个短式数据集和艺术与生命风格上最落后的目标为ListNet和LambdaRank,它们的设计是为了在检索中进行分级的正则相关性。 我们得出两个结论。 理直气壮的MSE是我们设置中一个有充分根据的默认,因为它在主标签中使用量度信息,在池大小中线性使用尺度,但是对偶的目标在本质上不是次优的,在平面上进行. 更重要的是,狭义的扩展证实,该框架的收益来自嵌入回收和火车时间候选规模,而不是损失,我们并不声称损失是一种贡献。

blocks.en: Table 5 compares our ranker with reward models that personalize by fitting or inferring user-specific parameters from labeled preference comparisons of the target user: PAL [ 9 ] , VPL [ 22 ] , PReF [ 30 ] , LoRe [ 2 ] , GPO [ 40 ] , and SynthesizeMe [ 27 ] . We evaluate on XRec, the only family in which such supervision can be constructed: its users recur across interactions, whereas every LaMP and LaMP-QA prompt belongs to a distinct user with a history but no preference labels, so for those tasks the strongest feasible heavyweight comparator is the reward model finetuned on the personalized training distribution reported in Section 4.3 .
blocks.zh: 表5比较了我们的分级符与奖励模型,这些模型通过从标注的用户偏好比较中安装或推导用户特定参数而实现个性化:PAL[9],VPL[22],PReF[30],Lore[2],GPO[40],以及合成Me[27]. 我们在XRec上评价了能够建立这种监督的唯一一家:其用户通过互动反复出现,而每个LAMP和LAMP-QA的提示属于一个不同的用户,该用户有历史,但没有首选标签,因此,对于这些任务来说,最可行的重量级比较者是第4.3节所报告的个性化培训分配调整的奖励模式。

blocks.en: We follow the official implementations and preserve the mechanism that defines each method, namely how its per-user parameters are obtained. For each evaluation user we hold out up to eight of their training interactions and mine labeled comparison pairs from the on-policy candidate pools of those interactions, with the chosen response being the candidate with higher ROUGE-L against that user’s reference. PAL, PReF, and LoRe fit their per-user vectors on these pairs by gradient descent or regularized logistic regression, with their shared prototypes or reward bases trained on the training-user population; VPL encodes the same pairs with its pair encoder to infer its latent user embedding; GPO meta-learns across users and receives the user’s labeled context interactions in context at test time; SynthesizeMe induces a persona from the same pairs and selects with a persona-prompted pairwise judge (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct) run as a single-elimination tournament over the pool. PAL, VPL, PReF, and LoRe operate on the same frozen generator embeddings as our ranker at a matched parameter budget of about 2.8M, with the official default configurations: two prompt-conditioned prototypes with a cosine ideal-point score for PAL, sixteen basis reward features for PReF, a rank-8 basis for LoRe, and the official 128-dimensional, six-layer transformer for GPO; SynthesizeMe runs the released package with a persona search budget of five to ten candidates per user. All methods select from the same Best-of-64 candidate pools and are evaluated on each user’s held-out test interaction. Our ranker receives only the content profile and zero preference labels.
blocks.zh: 我们跟踪官方的执行情况,并保留界定每一种方法的机制,即如何获得其每个用户的参数。 对于每个评估用户,我们最多可以进行8次培训互动,以及来自这些互动政策候选人库的、贴有地雷标签的对比对,所选择的答复是比该用户参考值更高的ROUGE-L的候选人。 PAL、PReF和Lore通过梯度下降或正规化的后勤回归,使这些对子上的用户矢量与他们共享的原型或奖励基础相匹配,对培训用户群进行培训; VPL用其配对编码器编码同样的对子,推断其潜在的用户嵌入; GPO元教育跨越用户,并在测试时接受用户标注的上下文互动; Synthesize Me从同一对子中诱导一个人,并选择一个由人推动的对子裁判员(Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct)在池上进行单消除比赛。 PAL,VPL,PReF,和Lore在与我们的对应参数预算约2.8M的同一种冷冻生成器嵌入上运行,官方默认配置:两个带有对PAL的余弦理想分数的快速条件原型,对PREF的十六个基础奖励功能,对Lore的八级基础,对GPO的128维六层正式变压器;SynthesizeMe运行发行的软件包,每个用户有5到10名候选人的人物搜索预算. 所有方法都从同一个最佳64名候选人库中挑选,并在每个用户的搁置测试互动中进行评价。 我们的排行榜只接收内容简介和零优先标签.

blocks.en: Our ranker matches the strongest reward-factorization baseline, VPL, within noise on all three datasets, while requiring no annotated pairs per user and no per-candidate encoder pass. PAL, PReF, and LoRe are below ours on every dataset. GPO obtains the highest raw scores, by about 0.005 ROUGE-L per dataset, but still depends on per-user labeled examples and on post-hoc scoring of materialized candidates. SynthesizeMe selects close to random: its persona-prompted judge captures 1–2% of the oracle headroom, and a generic judge without the persona is no worse (0.2033, 0.1677, and 0.1378 ROUGE-L on Amazon, Yelp, and Google), mirroring the miscalibration of generalist reward models in Section 4.2 . A further diagnostic explains why the user-conditioning machinery of these baselines does not pay off here: giving each user another user’s fitted parameters or context set changes the selection by at most 0.0008 ROUGE-L for every trained method, including ours. Because every candidate is generated with the user’s profile in the prompt, personalization is already realized at generation time, and what remains at selection is a calibrated judgment of which candidate comes closest to what the user would have written. This is precisely the judgment our lightweight ranker provides without any per-user labels, and it reinforces rather than competes with our central claim that the personalization headroom is a candidate matching problem.
blocks.zh: 我们的排位器匹配了所有三个数据集中最强的奖励系数基准,即VPL,同时不需要每个用户附加注释的对数,也不需要每个指定编码器通过. PAL,PReF,和Lore 在每个数据集都低于我们. GPO获得的原始分数最高,每套数据集得分约为0.005 ROUGE-L,但仍取决于每个用户贴上标签的例数以及实际考生的附加分数. 合成大小 我选择了近乎随机的:它的人格提示法官捕捉了1–2%的甲骨文头室,没有人格的普通法官也不逊色(0.2033,0.1677和0.1378 ROUGE-L on Amazon, Yelp, 和Google),这反映了第4.2节中通用主义奖励模型的误判. 还有一项诊断说明,为什么这些基线的用户调节机制不能在这里产生效果:给每个用户一个用户的适配参数或上下文,最多可以0.0008 ROUGE-L对包括我们在内的每一种训练有素的方法进行选择。 因为每个候选人都是用用户的简介在即时生成的,所以个性化在一代人的时间就已经实现,而选择时剩下的是校准判断哪个候选人最接近用户会写的东西. 这恰恰是我们轻量级无任何用户标签的判断,它强化了而不是与我们中央声称的个性化头室是一个候选匹配问题相竞争.

blocks.en: Given a document and the user’s history of past writings, the model produces a short user-styled text: a news headline for an article (News, 1,889 evaluation prompts), a title for a research-paper abstract (Scholarly, 2,498), or a rephrased tweet in the user’s voice (Tweet, 1,495). Following the benchmark’s retrieval-augmented protocol, the prompt carries the three profile items retrieved by BM25 for the current input, and the reference is the headline, title, or tweet the user actually wrote.

blocks.en: Given an open-ended information-seeking question and the asker’s narrative history, the model generates a long-form answer tailored to the asker’s background and needs, across three topical domains: Arts & Entertainment (Art), Lifestyle & Personal Development (Lifestyle), and Society & Culture (Society). The prompt follows the benchmark’s retrieval-augmented template with the six past questions retrieved by BM25. LaMP-QA ships rubrics rather than reference answers; we use, for each question, the per-user reference answer released with Personalized RewardBench [ 17 ] , whose question identifiers coincide with the LaMP-QA test set, and split the questions 90/10 into ranker training and evaluation (77, 99, and 108 evaluation prompts).

blocks.en: Given a user–item interaction together with the user profile and the item profile, the model generates a natural-language explanation of why the item suits the user, on three platforms (Amazon, Yelp, Google; 3,000 evaluation prompts each), with the user’s own review-style explanation as reference. We use the benchmark’s explainer prompt with its textual user and item summaries and generate with the plain instruction-tuned LLM, without the collaborative embedding tokens specific to XRec’s own model.

blocks.en: Table 8 reports measured wall-clock and memory costs on a single NVIDIA RTX A6000 (46 GiB) for one query with 64 candidates. Scoring the pool with the 2.8M-parameter ranker takes 0.098 ms at 0.93 GiB peak GPU memory, roughly 655k candidates per second, when the candidate embeddings are recycled from generation. Scoring the same pool with an 8B reward model takes 1.7–3.9 s at 18–22 GiB (mean 2.4 s over Skywork-Reward-V2, InternLM2, URM, and ArmoRM), a latency gap of four orders of magnitude and a memory gap of about 22 × 22\times . Our current implementation does not yet read the states off the generation pass but recomputes them in a separate pooling pass (Appendix C.2 ); counting that pass, end-to-end selection costs 2.1 ms per candidate, still 18 × 18\times cheaper than reward-model scoring, and the recycled figure is the architectural ceiling. The one-off cost of embedding a user’s profile is 7 ms (XRec), 96 ms (Scholarly), and 118 ms (LaMP-QA) per user when computed standalone and zero when recycled. For context, generating the pool itself costs 10 ms per candidate (0.65 s per query) on short-form generation and roughly an order of magnitude more on long-form QA (about 11 s per query), so generation rather than selection dominates the test-time budget, and scoring with an 8B reward model costs as much as generating the entire pool it evaluates. Ranking guided generation removes the need to materialize the pool at all: each intervention costs one forward and backward pass through the MLP plus one V × d V\times d matrix–vector product, which is negligible relative to a generator forward pass, and the gate fires on a minority of decoding steps (4–39% at the default threshold, Appendix C.3 ). Generation and embedding use vLLM, whereas the reward models run with HF transformers at batch size 32 as released, so part of the latency gap reflects serving implementation; the parameter and memory ratios do not.
blocks.zh: 表8报告对一个有64名候选人的NVIDIA RTX A6000(46 GiB)单次查询的墙上时间和内存成本进行了衡量。 用2.8M参数的分级器对游泳池进行分级,在0.93 GiB峰值GPU内存时需要0.098 ms,每秒约655k候选人,当候选嵌入物从一代中回收时. 以8B奖励型号对同一个游泳池进行校对,在18–22 GiB时需要1.7–3.9 s(比Skywork-Reward-V2,InternLM2,URM,和ArmoRM要多2.4 s),一个4个量级的悬空和大约22×22\时的内存空. 我们目前的实施还没有将州从一代人通行证上读出,而是在单独的集合证(附录C.2)中重新计算;计算通过,每个候选人的端对端选择费用为2.1毫秒,仍然比奖励模式评分便宜18×18×次,回收的数字是建筑上限. 嵌入用户配置的一次性费用为7毫秒(XRec)、96毫秒(Scholarly)和每个用户独立计算时118毫秒(LAMP-QA),回收时为零。 就上下文而言,生成池本身在短式生成时每候选人花费10毫秒(每查询0.65秒),在长式QA(每查询约11秒)上,大致是一个数量级的顺序,因此生成而不是选择在测试时间预算上占据主导地位,并以8B的奖励模式成本评分,与生成它评价的整个池一样多. 排名制导的一代完全不需要实现集合:每次干预都花费一个前向和后向通过MLP+一个V × d V\times d matrium - vector产品,相对于一个发电机前向通道来说是微不足道的,门对少数解码步骤(默认阈值为4-39%,附录C.3)开火. 生成和嵌入使用vLLM,而奖励型号则在释放时以第32批大小的HF变压器运行,因此部分延迟差距反映了服务执行;参数和内存比率没有.

blocks.en: 1. Claims Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Abstract and introduction Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A [No] or [N/A] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper. 2. Limitations Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Section 5 Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations. 3. Theory assumptions and proofs Question: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and a complete (and correct) proof? Answer: [N/A] Justification: [N/A] Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include theoretical results. • All the theorems, formulas, and proofs in the paper should be numbered and cross-referenced. • All assumptions should be clearly stated or referenced in the statement of any theorems. • The proofs can either appear in the main paper or the supplemental material, but if they appear in the supplemental material, the authors are encouraged to provide a short proof sketch to provide intuition. • Inversely, any informal proof provided in the core of the paper should be complemented by formal proofs provided in appendix or supplemental material. • Theorems and Lemmas that the proof relies upon should be properly referenced. 4. Experimental result reproducibility Question: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Section 4 Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results. 5. Open access to data and code Question: Does the paper provide open access to the data and code, with sufficient instructions to faithfully reproduce the main experimental results, as described in supplemental material? Answer: [Yes] Justification: after authorlist Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that paper does not include experiments requiring code. • Please see the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be possible, so [No] is an acceptable answer. Papers cannot be rejected simply for not including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source benchmark). • The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce the results. See the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • The authors should provide instructions on data access and preparation, including how to access the raw data, preprocessed data, intermediate data, and generated data, etc. • The authors should provide scripts to reproduce all experimental results for the new proposed method and baselines. If only a subset of experiments are reproducible, they should state which ones are omitted from the script and why. • At submission time, to preserve anonymity, the authors should release anonymized versions (if applicable). • Providing as much information as possible in supplemental material (appended to the paper) is recommended, but including URLs to data and code is permitted. 6. Experimental setting/details Question: Does the paper specify all the training and test details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen, type of optimizer) necessary to understand the results? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Section 4 Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The experimental setting should be presented in the core of the paper to a level of detail that is necessary to appreciate the results and make sense of them. • The full details can be provided either with the code, in appendix, or as supplemental material. 7. Experiment statistical significance Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Section 4 Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The authors should answer [Yes] if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper. • The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions). • The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.) • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors). • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean. • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text. 8. Experiments compute resources Question: For each experiment, does the paper provide sufficient information on the computer resources (type of compute workers, memory, time of execution) needed to reproduce the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Appendix C.2/C.4 Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The paper should indicate the type of compute workers CPU or GPU, internal cluster, or cloud provider, including relevant memory and storage. • The paper should provide the amount of compute required for each of the individual experimental runs as well as estimate the total compute. • The paper should disclose whether the full research project required more compute than the experiments reported in the paper (e.g., preliminary or failed experiments that didn’t make it into the paper). 9. Code of ethics Question: Does the research conducted in the paper conform, in every respect, with the NeurIPS Code of Ethics https://neurips.cc/public/EthicsGuidelines ? Answer: [Yes] Justification: reviewed Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the authors have not reviewed the NeurIPS Code of Ethics. • If the authors answer [No] , they should explain the special circumstances that require a deviation from the Code of Ethics. • The authors should make sure to preserve anonymity (e.g., if there is a special consideration due to laws or regulations in their jurisdiction). 10. Broader impacts Question: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative societal impacts of the work performed? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Personalized generation is directly related to societal impacts. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that there is no societal impact of the work performed. • If the authors answer [N/A] or [No] , they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact. • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations. • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster. • The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology. • If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML). 11. Safeguards Question: Does the paper describe safeguards that have been put in place for responsible release of data or models that have a high risk for misuse (e.g., pre-trained language models, image generators, or scraped datasets)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: [N/A] Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper poses no such risks. • Released models that have a high risk for misuse or dual-use should be released with necessary safeguards to allow for controlled use of the model, for example by requiring that users adhere to usage guidelines or restrictions to access the model or implementing safety filters. • Datasets that have been scraped from the Internet could pose safety risks. The authors should describe how they avoided releasing unsafe images. • We recognize that providing effective safeguards is challenging, and many papers do not require this, but we encourage authors to take this into account and make a best faith effort. 12. Licenses for existing assets Question: Are the creators or original owners of assets (e.g., code, data, models), used in the paper, properly credited and are the license and terms of use explicitly mentioned and properly respected? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Section 4.1 Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not use existing assets. • The authors should cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset. • The authors should state which version of the asset is used and, if possible, include a URL. • The name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) should be included for each asset. • For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of service of that source should be provided. • If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. For popular datasets, paperswithcode.com/datasets has curated licenses for some datasets. Their licensing guide can help determine the license of a dataset. • For existing datasets that are re-packaged, both the original license and the license of the derived asset (if it has changed) should be provided. • If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to the asset’s creators. 13. New assets Question: Are new assets introduced in the paper well documented and is the documentation provided alongside the assets? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We release our code repo. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not release new assets. • Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their submissions via structured templates. This includes details about training, license, limitations, etc. • The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose asset is used. • At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable). You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file. 14. Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects Question: For crowdsourcing experiments and research with human subjects, does the paper include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable, as well as details about compensation (if any)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: [N/A] Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper. • According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector. 15. Institutional review board (IRB) approvals or equivalent for research with human subjects Question: Does the paper describe potential risks incurred by study participants, whether such risks were disclosed to the subjects, and whether Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals (or an equivalent approval/review based on the requirements of your country or institution) were obtained? Answer: [N/A] Justification: [N/A] Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Depending on the country in which research is conducted, IRB approval (or equivalent) may be required for any human subjects research. If you obtained IRB approval, you should clearly state this in the paper. • We recognize that the procedures for this may vary significantly between institutions and locations, and we expect authors to adhere to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and the guidelines for their institution. • For initial submissions, do not include any information that would break anonymity (if applicable), such as the institution conducting the review. 16. Declaration of LLM usage Question: Does the paper describe the usage of LLMs if it is an important, original, or non-standard component of the core methods in this research? Note that if the LLM is used only for writing, editing, or formatting purposes and does not impact the core methodology, scientific rigor, or originality of the research, declaration is not required. Answer: [Yes] Justification: Section 3 Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the core method development in this research does not involve LLMs as any important, original, or non-standard components. • Please refer to our LLM policy in the NeurIPS handbook for what should or should not be described.
blocks.zh: 一、导 言 索赔问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了文件的贡献和范围? 答复:[是] 说明:摘要和导言 抽象和(或)导言应明确说明所提出的要求,包括文件中的贡献以及重要的假设和限制。 审议人员不会很好地看待对这一问题的[否]或[无]答复。 所提出的主张应与理论和实验结果相符,并反映在多大程度上可以预期结果可以归纳到其他场合。 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。 2. 限制问题: 文件是否讨论了作者所做工作的限制? 答复:[是] 说明:第5节 准则: 答案[无/A]意味着文件没有限制,而答案[无]则意味着文件有限制,但在文件中没有讨论这些限制。 鼓励作者在论文中另辟一个“限制”部分。 文件应说明任何强有力的假设,以及这些假设遭到违反(例如,独立性假设、无噪声设置、模型精确度、不对称近似只在当地持有)的结果如何有力。 作者应思考这些假设在实践中可能如何遭到违反,其影响如何。 作者应反思所提出主张的范围,例如,如果这种办法只在几个数据集或几个运行中测试。 一般来说,经验性结果往往取决于隐含的假设,这些假设应当加以阐述。 作者应反思影响该办法执行的因素。 例如,一个面部识别算法在图像分辨率低或图像在低光照下拍摄时可能表现不佳. 或语音对文本系统可能无法可靠地用于为在线讲座提供闭门字幕,因为它无法处理技术术语。 作者应讨论拟议算法的计算效率,以及它们如何用数据集大小来衡量。 如果适用,作者应讨论他们处理隐私和公平问题的办法可能存在的局限性。 虽然作者可能担心审查人员会以完全诚实的限度作为拒绝的理由,但更糟糕的结果可能是审查人员发现文件中不承认的限制。 作者应运用最佳判断,承认有利于透明度的个别行动在制定维护社会完整性的规范方面发挥着重要作用。 将特别指示审查人员不要惩罚在限制方面的诚实。 3. 理论假设和证明 问题: 对于每一项理论结果,论文是否提供了一整套假设和完整的(和正确的)证明? 回答:[N/A] 理由说明:[N/A] 准则: • 答案[N/A] 表示论文不包括理论结果. • 支助 所有论文中的定理,公式和证明,都应该编号,相互参照. • 支助 所有假设都应在任何定理的说明中明确说明或提及。 证据可以出现在主要论文或补充材料中,但如果在补充材料中出现,则鼓励作者提供简短的证据草图以提供直觉. • 反之,文件核心中提供的任何非正式证据都应辅以附录或补充材料中提供的正式证据。 • 应适当参考证据所依据的定理和莱玛。 4. 实验结果可复制 问题: 文件是否充分披露复制文件主要实验结果所需的所有信息,以影响文件的主要主张和/或结论(无论是否提供代码和数据)? 答复:[是] 说明:第4节 准则: 答案[不适用/A]是指论文不包括实验。 如果论文包括实验,审查人员将不会很好地看待对这一问题的回答: 使文件可以复制很重要,无论是否提供代码和数据。 如果资料是数据集和/或模型,作者应说明为使结果可以复制或可核查而采取的步骤。 • 根据贡献情况,可采用各种方式实现可复制性。 例如,如果这种贡献是一种新颖的架构,充分描述这种架构可能就足够了,或者如果这种贡献是一个具体的模型和经验性评价,那么就可能有必要使其他人有可能用同样的数据集复制这个模型,或者提供对模型的访问. 总论中. 释放代码和数据往往是实现这一点的好方法,但也可以通过详细指示来提供可复制性,说明如何复制结果,访问主机模型(如在大语言模型的情况下),释放模型检查点,或者其他适合进行的研究的手段. • 支助 虽然NeurIPS并不要求发布代码,但会议确实要求所有提交材料都为可复制性提供某种合理的途径,这可能取决于贡献的性质. 例如(a) 如果贡献主要是一种新的算法,则论文应当明确说明如何复制该算法。 (b) 如果贡献主要是新的示范结构,文件应清楚、全面地描述这种结构。 (c) 如果贡献是一个新的模型(例如大语言模型),那么应该有一种方法来访问这个模型来复制结果,或者有一种方法来复制模型(例如,有一个开源数据集或关于如何构建数据集的指示). (d) 我们认识到,在某些情况下,可复制性可能很困难,在这种情况下,欢迎作者描述它们为可复制性规定的具体方式。 对于封闭源代码模型,可能以某种方式(如注册用户)限制对模型的获取,但其他研究者应该有一定途径复制或验证结果. 5. 开放存取数据和代码问题: 文件是否提供了开放的数据和代码,并有足够的指示,如补充材料所述,忠实地复制主要的实验结果? 答复:[是] 理由说明:在作者名单之后 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括需要代码的实验。 详情请见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmission Policy)。 虽然我们鼓励发布代码和数据,但我们理解这也许是不可能的,因此[否]是一个可以接受的答案. 不能仅仅因为没有包含代码而拒绝文件,除非这是贡献的核心(例如,对于一个新的开源基准). • 支助 指示应包含复制结果所需的准确命令和环境。 详情见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy)。 作者应提供关于数据存取和准备的说明,包括如何获取原始数据、预先处理的数据、中间数据以及生成的数据等。 作者应提供脚本,复制所有实验结果,用于新的拟议方法和基线。 如果只有一组实验可以复制,它们应该说明哪些实验从脚本中删除,以及为什么。 在提交来文时,为保留匿名性,提交人应公布匿名版本(如适用)。 • 建议在补充材料中提供尽可能多的信息(附于文件),但允许将URL纳入数据和代码。 6. 实验设置/细节问题: 文件是否具体说明了解结果所需的所有培训和测试细节(如数据分割、超参数、如何选择、优化者的类型)? 答复:[是] 说明:第4节 准则: 答案[不适用/A]是指论文不包括实验。 实验环境应在文件核心中详细介绍,以便了解结果,使之合理。 详细情况可通过附录中的代码或补充材料提供。 7. 实验统计意义 问题: 纸质报告错误是否含有适当和正确定义的信息或关于实验统计意义的其他适当信息? 答复:[是] 说明:第4节 准则: 答案[不适用/A]是指论文不包括实验。 如果结果附有错误栏、信任间隔或统计意义测试,至少对于支持论文主要主张的实验,作者应回答[是]。 应明确说明错误条所捕获的变异因素(例如,列车/测试拆分、初始化、随机绘制某些参数,或在特定实验条件下的总体运行)。 计算错误栏的方法应当加以解释(封闭的表单公式、调用库函数、靴子陷阱等) • 应给出假设(例如,通常分布错误)。 应明确误差栏是标准偏差还是平均值的标准误差. ^ 报告1-西格玛错误栏是正常的,但应该说明这一点。 如果错误的正常性假设没有得到核实,提交人最好报告2-西格玛错误栏,而不是说他们有96%的CI。 • 支助 对于不对称分布,作者应注意不要在表格或数字对称误差栏中显示会产生超出范围的结果(如负误差率). • 支助 如果在表格或图中报告错误栏,作者应在文字中解释它们是如何计算的,并在文字中参考相应的数字或表格。 8. 实验计算资源 问题:对于每个实验,论文是否提供了复制实验所需的计算机资源(计算工人类型,内存,执行时间)的充分信息? 答复:[是] 理由说明:附录C.2/C.4 · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 纸张应说明计算工人的CPU或GPU、内部集群或云提供商的类型,包括相关的内存和存储。 文件应提供每次试验所需的计算数额,并估计计算总额。 论文应披露完整的研究项目是否比论文中报告的实验需要更多的计算(例如初步或失败的实验,这些实验没有把它写进论文中). 9. 道德守则问题:文件中进行的研究是否在各个方面都符合《新IPS道德守则》(https://neurips.cc/public/Ethics Guidelines)? 答复:[是] 理由:经过审查的准则: 答案[不详]意味着作者没有审查《新IPS道德守则》。 如果作者回答[否],他们应该解释需要偏离道德守则的特殊情况。 提交人应确保匿名(例如,如果由于其管辖范围内的法律或条例而得到特别考虑)。 10. 更广泛的影响问题:本文件是否讨论所开展工作的潜在积极社会影响和消极社会影响? 回答:[是]说明:个性化的一代与社会影响直接相关。 · 答案[N/A]是指所进行的工作没有社会影响。 如果作者回答[N/A]或[否],他们应当解释他们的工作为何没有社会影响,或为何文件没有涉及社会影响。 • 支助 负面社会影响的例子包括潜在的恶意或意外使用(例如:造谣、制造假面貌、监视)、公平考虑(例如:采用可能作出对特定群体造成不公平影响的决定的技术)、隐私考虑和安全考虑。 会议期望许多文件将是基础研究,而不是与特定应用挂钩,更不用说部署. 然而,如果有任何否定性申请的直接途径,提交人应当指出。 例如,可以合理地指出,可以利用基因模型质量的提高来产生用于造谣的Deepfakes. 另一方面,不需要指出优化神经网络的通用算法可以让人们训练出更快生成Deepfake的模型.  • 作者应考虑在技术作为预期和正确使用时可能产生的伤害,在技术作为预期使用时可能产生的伤害,但产生不正确的结果,以及因(有意或无意)滥用技术而造成的伤害。 如果存在负面的社会影响,作者还可以讨论可能的缓解战略(例如,对模型进行封闭释放,在攻击之外提供防御,监测误用的机制,监测系统如何从反馈中学习的机制,提高ML的效率和可获取性)。 11. 保障问题: 文件是否描述了为负责任地发布具有高度滥用风险的数据或模型(例如,经过预先培训的语言模型、图像生成器或报废数据集)而实施的保障措施? 回答:[无/A] 理由说明:[无/A]准则: 答案[无/A]意味着该文件没有构成这种风险。 • 释放的具有高度滥用或双重用途风险的模型,应附带必要的保障措施,允许控制使用该模型,例如要求用户遵守使用准则或限制使用该模型或实施安全过滤器。 • 支助 从互联网上拆掉的数据集可能构成安全风险。 作者应说明如何避免释放不安全的图像。 我们认识到,提供有效的保障是一项挑战,许多文件并不要求这样做,但我们鼓励作者考虑到这一点,并作出最大的诚意努力。 12. 现有资产的许可证问题: 纸上是否使用资产(例如代码、数据、模型)的创造者或原始所有人,是否适当贷记,许可证和使用条款是否明确提及和适当遵守? 答复:[是] 理由:第4.1节 准则: 答案[不详]是指该文件不使用现有资产。 作者应引述产生代码包或数据集的原始文件。 作者应说明使用哪个版本的资产,并在可能的情况下包括一个URL。 许可证名称(如CC-BY 4.0)应包含每项资产。 • 支助 对于从某一特定来源(如网站)提取的数据,应当提供该来源的版权和服务条件。 资产放行的,应当提供许可证,著作权信息,包件中的使用条件. 对于流行的数据集来说,使用code.com/dataset的论文拥有一些数据集的许可证。 它们的许可证指南有助于确定一个数据集的许可证。 • 支助 对于重新包装的现有数据集,应提供原始许可证和衍生资产的许可证(如果已经改变)。 如果这种信息不在网上提供,则鼓励作者接触资产的创造者。 13. 新资产问题:文件中介绍的新资产是否有详细记录,是否与资产一起提供文件? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们公布密码 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不释放新资产。 • 研究人员应通过结构化模板将数据集/编码/模型的细节作为提交材料的一部分。 • 培训、许可证、限制等细节 该文件应讨论是否以及如何获得资产被使用者的同意。 在提交时,请记住对您的资产进行匿名(如果适用)。 您可以创建一个匿名的 URL 或者包含一个匿名的 zip 文件 。 14. 人口集中和人类课题研究 关于众包实验和与人类主体的研究,论文是否包括提供给参与者的指示全文和(如果适用的话)截图,以及(如果有)补偿的细节? 回答:[n/A] 理由:[n/A] 准则: • 答案[n/A] 表示论文不涉及众包,也不涉及对人类主体的研究. • 将这一资料列入补充材料是好的,但如果论文的主要贡献涉及人类主题,那么应在主要文件中尽可能详细。 • 支助 根据《新IPS道德守则》,从事数据收集、管理或其他工作的工人应至少得到数据收集者的本国最低工资。 15. 机构审查委员会(IRB)批准或相当于与人有关的研究 文件是否描述了研究参与者可能面临的风险,是否向主体披露了这些风险,以及是否获得了机构审查委员会的批准(或根据贵国或机构的要求获得同等的批准/审查)? 回答:[n/A] 理由:[n/A] 准则: • 答案[n/A] 表示论文不涉及众包,也不涉及对人类主体的研究. • 视进行研究的国家而定,任何人类课题研究可能需要IRB批准(或相当于批准)。 如果得到移民和难民局的批准,应在报纸上明确说明这一点。 我们认识到,各机构和地点在这方面的程序可能大不相同,我们期望作者遵守《新IPS道德守则》及其机构准则。 • 支助 对于初次提交材料,不包括任何可能打破匿名性(如果适用)的信息,例如进行审查的机构。 16. 关于LLM使用的声明问题: 论文是否描述了LLMs的使用,如果它是本研究核心方法的重要、原始或非标准组成部分? 请注意,如果LLM只用于写作,编辑或格式化目的,且不影响研究的核心方法,科学严谨性或独创性,则不需要声明. 答复:[是] 理由说明:第3节 准则: 答案[N/A]是指本研究的核心方法开发并不涉及LLMs作为任何重要、原始或非标准的组成部分。 请参看NeurIPS手册中我们的LLM政策,说明应该或不应该描述什么。

blocks.zh: 索偿

blocks.en: Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope?
blocks.zh: 问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了文件的贡献和范围?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: Abstract and introduction
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 摘要和导言

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A [No] or [N/A] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案[N/A]是指摘要和导言不包括文件中提出的要求。 抽象和(或)导言应明确说明所提出的要求,包括文件中的贡献以及重要的假设和限制。 审议人员不会很好地看待对这一问题的[否]或[无]答复。 所提出的主张应与理论和实验结果相符,并反映在多大程度上可以预期结果可以归纳到其他场合。 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。

blocks.zh: 所提出的索赔应当与理论和实验结果相符,并反映在多大程度上可以预期结果能够归纳到其他环境。

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件是否讨论了作者所做工作的限制?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: Section 5
blocks.zh: 理由说明:第5节

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations.
